🔔 Can DATA Network bring lasting activity to Sui? 

📣 DATA Network plans to retire its independent chain and run its AI training data registry on Sui, with Walrus handling files. Sui Foundation is investing $30 million in the network. A registry that its backers say already records millions of receipts daily could bring activity to Sui; how much of that translates into recurring SUI demand remains an open question.

⭐️ Sui Foundation’s October 12 announcement  says Trace, a rights registry for AI training data, is joining its stack. Walrus will store encrypted original files and Sui will record programmable rights and settlements. DATA Network’s own chain will eventually close. The foundation says its $30 million commitment makes it the largest institutional holder of the DATA Network, alongside PIP Labs and the DATA Foundation. The statement does not publish a completed migration date or a dollar amount of fees the business expects to pay on Sui. 

⚠️ Trace registers a data contribution, its origin and the rights attached to it. The foundation says the system has processed more than 250 million contributions since a June launch and averages over 3 million receipts a day. Applications named in the announcement include Kled, Numo and Oto. Kled is described as an opt in human data marketplace with more than 1.5 billion records being onboarded. Those are participant supplied operational claims; the release does not contain an independently audited breakdown by customer, chain, fee or paying AI lab. 

🔖 DATA Foundation says Trace settles payments to contributors when their data is licensed. A nurse’s consented account, a dashcam clip or a factory worker’s demonstration might be recorded as training material with use rights. The registry entry is not necessarily the complete source file. Its design separates a claim about who supplied data and who may use it from storage of the bytes. Sui and Walrus are meant to handle those parts after migration.

As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the Cisco Expressway Series software engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in a software hardening release that addresses multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.  
These vulnerabilities were found during internal testing and are not known to be actively exploited. To assist customers in patching and streamline the disclosure process, Cisco has grouped these issues by their underlying vulnerability class - Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) - and assigned a single Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier (CVE ID) to each CWE grouping.
Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices.
Note: Cisco may publish separate security advisories that provide additional details about individual vulnerabilities that are addressed in this release.
Cisco has released a software update that addresses these vulnerabilities. There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities.
This advisory is available at the following link:
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-exwy-hardening-FhcqBVcs
This advisory is part of a group of advisories. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of October 21, 2026, Security Advisories (https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-notice-QGwHnJ6k).

📡 Iran MP warns enemies of more painful response to any new threat

📌 Jiroft, IRNA – Chairman of Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, Ebrahim Azizi has warned that any new hostile action against the country would draw a more painful response.

Any reckless, miscalculated or repeated mistake by the enemy will certainly impose far heavier, more painful and more costly consequences than before, Azizi said on Thursday.
​
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony of an independent police command in southern Kerman Province, Azizi said the new command sent a message that security rested on public support and the Iranian people’s unwavering resolve.
​
Azizi said Iran’s Armed Forces, including the Army, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) and the Law Enforcement Command, remained committed to defending the country.
​
He said adversaries were seeking to undermine the Islamic Republic’s credibility and legitimacy, adding that Iranian officials’ commitment to promises and honest service would strengthen public trust and institutional legitimacy.
​
He also recalled the assassination of Brigadier General Qassem Soleimani and other resistance commanders and officials, saying their martyrdom would not be forgotten.
​
He described the establishment of the southern Kerman command as an initial step toward strengthening security across southeastern Iran, saying that sustainable national security required a comprehensive approach to border regions.
